items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: It was a child movie star discovered by, I think it was Eddie Cantor, named Bobby Breen.

ctx.x: I play drums. But I learned from Art Tatum to hear every note in the chord. Because he would make me sing. Like when I was 13, he used to say, “sing this” [scats]. And I’d go, “huh?” But then I used to have to come by his house when we started working together in © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

this club, two shows a night. You know I was billed. I had billing. “Little Jonny Hendricks — the Sepia Bobby Breen.” It was a child movie star discovered by, I think it was Eddie Cantor, named Bobby Breen. He made a couple of pictures. One was “Rhythm on the River” and he was a very big star there for a hot minute. And so they named me “Little Jonny Hendricks, the Sepia of Bobby Breen,” accompanied by Art Tatum. I mean I’ve got one of those bills.
I was going to ask. I hope you do.
